title: RAW wine briefly retains its arrangement after vessel destruction under a relative-rate explanation
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED_NOT_SELECTED_NOT_EXECUTED. Megenberg's Seneca-attributed vessel break leaves wine briefly together; faster impact than dispersal explains the delay, an intact open-glass analogy supports it, and viscosity is only possible additional help. Preserve object continuity, finite duration and unequal evidential status without treating the analogy as a second broken vessel.

design.mechanism: A Seneca-attributed event breaks a wine vessel while the wine briefly remains together without it, as it had stood in the vessel. The source explains this through the strike being too fast for the wine to disperse as quickly. It then compares rapid whirling of an open wine/water glass without spillage, and tentatively adds that the wine may have been viscous, which also helped. Keep the broken-container event and intact-container analogy distinct, preserve the relative-rate comparison and short duration, and keep possible viscosity additional rather than certain or necessary.
design.contrast: R1: breaking support entails immediate disappearance or dispersal of its contents. R2: the wine remains together permanently after the vessel breaks. R3: the thunder secretly removes wine from an undamaged vessel, as in a different Clarum story. R4: the whirled glass is also broken or the report establishes one physically identical mechanism in both examples. R5: viscosity is observed, certain, necessary or the sole cause. R6: the text reports a measured delay and an observed later dispersal event.
design.prediction: A faithful account must allow the same wine to remain together for a short while after the vessel breaks, comparing its temporary arrangement with the earlier contained state, while attributing that lag to the faster strike versus slower dispersal. The later analogy still owns an open intact glass and may involve wine OR water. Converting possible viscosity into a definite cause, removing the short duration, or reversing which of vessel and contents disappears changes the account. Container and wine labels alone do not preserve the temporal and evidential construction.
whole_source_duties: Exact complete local scope94.7 beginning Seneca spricht through94.15 ending daz hât auch dar zuo geholfen; the next Nu maht dû frâgen opens the separate seasonal argument.
The main event is attributed to Seneca in his time. It is not this producer's observation, a modern demonstration or an independently verified occurrence.

Thunder breaks a vessel full of wine; the wine remains together briefly without the vessel as it had stood in the vessel. Same-wine identity and the before/after comparator are explicit; no individual molecular identity or indefinite stable shape is proved.

The proposed cause is comparative timing: the strike was so fast that the wine could not disperse so quickly. The text gives no measured time, speed, viscosity or later observed endpoint of dispersal. No universal support-removal law or modern inertia account is supplied.

The supporting analogy is an open glass with wine OR water rapidly whirled in a sling or hand so nothing flows out. It retains its glass; it is not a second observed container-destruction event. Intact is descriptive shorthand for an analogy that retains its glass and does not state a break, not a separately inspected structural property of an actual vessel.

The separate possible explanation auch ist der wein leiht zæh gewesen is uncertain viscosity, with a further contribution. Do not promote it to observed necessity, guaranteed sufficiency or sole cause.

This passage differs from95.7–12 Clarum wine removal with vessel footprints, and from92.23–30 hard/soft selective damage. Those whole-source claims remain, but this card is not a swapped-object version of either.

Full chapter formation, perception, injury, warning, seasonal and classification claims stay linked through the frozen complete notes. This local offer is not a whole-chapter translation or a target-support continuity claim.
